repo_model.summary: This repository is a RelBench generic-search candidate workspace: main.py loads task and split tables from the sanitized cache and emits family-specific predictions, while kapso_evaluation/grader.py runs the candidate in isolation, validates outputs, scores validation predictions, and archives full runs.

entrypoints.how_to_run: python main.py --debug for the debug/fast candidate invocation, or python main.py for the full invocation.

where_to_edit.role: Primary candidate implementation; the file explicitly identifies the current code as a trivial baseline intended to be replaced.
Reusable task-loading, cache-access, prediction-saving, temporal-safety, and MAP@K helper functions.
Local prediction contract checker to run after generating output files.
Immutable evaluation and archiving pipeline; do not reimplement it or modify files under kapso_evaluation.

claims.statement: The candidate entrypoint is task-agnostic: it reads the dataset and task from environment variables, loads the RelBench task with download=False, sizes predictions from the validation and test tables, and detects rolling ticks from an empty or missing cached val.parquet file.

evidence.description: Reads RELBENCH_DATASET from the environment.
Loads the task with download=False.
Builds the cached validation parquet path.
Uses the cached validation table when present and otherwise treats the validation count as zero.
Marks the invocation as rolling when the validation count is zero.

claims.statement: Prediction generation dispatches by task family: recommendations receive repeated ranked destination IDs, binary classification receives 0.5 probabilities, multiclass classification receives uniform class scores, and other tasks receive the median training target.

evidence.description: Branches for RecommendationTask.
Creates a ranked integer row for recommendation predictions.
Branches for binary classification.
Branches for multiclass classification.
Uses the training table for the remaining task types.
Computes the median target used for regression-like predictions.

claims.statement: kapso_datasets.common provides the intended task-loading and output-writing abstraction: it loads the dataset, task, database, and train/val/test tables from the sanitized cache, and save_predictions writes both prediction arrays to the run directory.

Writes validation and test prediction files.

claims.statement: The grader runs main.py as an isolated subprocess, passes the run output directory through KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR, loads the resulting validation predictions, evaluates them with the official task evaluator, and requires the configured primary metric.

evidence.description: Defines candidate execution.
Invokes main.py and adds --debug for fast fidelity.
Injects KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR into the child environment.
Starts the candidate in a subprocess.

Computes official validation metrics.

claims.statement: Full-fidelity runs are archived with validation and test prediction artifacts, private metrics, a selection label, and a snapshot of candidate code; the manifest records the validation score and archive identifier.

evidence.description: Defines full-run archiving.
Copies prediction artifacts into the archive.
Writes archived validation and test metric metadata.
Creates the archive selection label.
Begins candidate code snapshotting.
Builds the machine-readable evaluation manifest.
Stores the primary validation metric as the manifest score.

claims.statement: Every ordinary run must write val_predictions.npy and test_predictions.npy under KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR, with rows positionally aligned to the task validation and test tables; validation predictions must be out-of-sample and must not use validation labels for training.

evidence.description: Requires both prediction files after every run.
Requires positional row alignment.
Requires validation predictions to be out-of-sample.
Restricts train-plus-validation usage to the model producing test predictions.

claims.statement: Expected prediction formats are binary float vectors in [0,1], regression float vectors, multiclass float matrices with one column per class, and recommendation integer matrices of shape (N,K) containing ranked destination IDs.

evidence.description: Defines binary and regression prediction shapes and binary probability bounds.
Defines multiclass and recommendation shapes and types.
Requires recommendation IDs to be ranked, distinct, and in the destination range.

claims.statement: The search score is the official validation primary metric; test labels are absent from the sanitized cache and test metrics cannot be observed in this evaluation loop.

evidence.description: Defines the official validation primary metric as the search score.
States that test metrics are private.

Places the primary validation metric in the manifest score.

evidence.description: Requires RelBench API access with download=False.
Documents loading from the sanitized cache.

Defines fast fidelity as main.py --debug.

claims.statement: After predictions are written, run python kapso_datasets/check_predictions.py; success is indicated by per-split OK messages followed by '[check_predictions] all checks passed'.

evidence.description: Recommends running the prediction checker before harness scoring.
Prints an OK message for each checked split.
Prints the all-checks-passed success message.

evidence.description: Prints official validation metrics.

claims.statement: Rolling-harness ticks intentionally have an empty validation table: main.py omits val_predictions.npy for that per-tick invocation, and the grader later assembles test and validation vectors from all tick outputs.

evidence.description: Documents the empty validation table in rolling snapshots.

claims.statement: The checked-in implementation is deliberately trivial: every recommendation row is identical, classification predictions are fixed priors, and regression-like predictions are a single training-target median; --debug only appears in the status print and does not select a different prediction algorithm.

evidence.description: Describes the outputs as trivial predictions.
Tiles the same recommendation row across all rows.
Uses a constant 0.5 binary prediction.
Uses uniform multiclass scores.
Uses a constant median regression prediction.
Uses --debug only in the printed status message.

claims.statement: The local checker warns rather than fails for recommendation IDs outside the destination range or duplicate IDs, so those warnings must be treated as correctness failures even though the process can report success.

evidence.description: Checks recommendation ID bounds.
Reports out-of-range IDs as a warning.
Counts duplicate recommendation rows.
Reports duplicate IDs as a warning.

claims.statement: In the grader's load_and_score path, both prediction files are required to exist, but the detailed shape and finite-value validation shown there is applied to validation predictions; use the standalone checker to validate both splits before relying on test artifacts.

Checks validation length and finiteness.

claims.statement: The evaluation suite is designed to run with Python plus relbench and numpy installed and does not require additional setup beyond a fast dry run.

evidence.description: States that the grader imports only standard library, numpy, and relbench.
Introduces the required environment.
States that Python with relbench and numpy is sufficient.

claims.statement: Runtime identity and output/cache locations arrive through RELBENCH_DATASET, RELBENCH_TASK, RELBENCH_CACHE_DIR, and KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR; the grader additionally requires the primary metric, work directory, timeout, and shared-cache variables.

book.summary: This repository is a RelBench generic-search candidate workspace: main.py loads task and split tables from the sanitized cache and emits family-specific predictions, while kapso_evaluation/grader.py runs the candidate in isolation, validates outputs, scores validation predictions, and archives full runs.

toc.title: Architecture
toc.one_liner: Task loading, prediction dispatch, contract validation, and official scoring are separated across the candidate, starter helpers, and immutable grader.

toc.title: Entrypoints
toc.one_liner: Run the candidate directly or invoke the provided grader for fast and full evaluation.

toc.title: Where to edit
toc.one_liner: Replace the baseline logic in main.py and use the starter helpers for contract-safe integration.

toc.title: Invariants
toc.one_liner: Prediction files, shapes, leakage rules, and scoring semantics are fixed by the evaluation contract.

toc.title: Testing
toc.one_liner: Use the fast grader for an end-to-end sanity check and the prediction checker for local shape and dtype validation.

toc.title: Gotchas
toc.one_liner: Rolling snapshots, baseline defaults, and checker warning behavior can produce results that look valid but are not competitive or fully enforced.

toc.title: Dependencies
toc.one_liner: The runtime depends on Python, NumPy, RelBench, and environment-provided task/cache configuration.
